raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On a PD decode server with the overlap scheduler, a retracted request's KV restored on resume can be overwritten by a forward that is still running. This holds for both retraction backups (`--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup host_pool` or `cpu_tensor`; one of them is picked by default).

The decode event loop processes step N-1's results only after launching step N. A request that finished in step N-1 is still in batch N, so that forward writes the KV of its last token into a slot the request owned. Its slots, that one included, go back to the allocator when step N-1's result is processed (the decode radix cache is off by default). In the next iteration, `process_decode_queue` -> `DecodePreallocQueue.resume_retracted_reqs` can allocate those slots to a resumed request, and `restore_kv_cache` copies the backup into them:
- the `host_pool` backend issues a host-to-device copy on the L2 transfer stream, ordered only after an event on the scheduler stream;
- the `cpu_tensor` backend copies on the scheduler stream.

The scheduler stream does not wait for forward N's KV writes. `_apply_war_barrier` waits only for the forward's shared reads, unless it falls back to the coarse barrier. So the restore can land first, and forward N then overwrites a restored token with the finished request's KV. The resumed request continues decoding with one corrupted token in its context.

The prebuilt path in `get_new_prebuilt_batch` already drains the in-flight forward for the same reason, from #35748: `self.schedule_stream.wait_stream(self.forward_stream)` before a prebuilt request seeds a possibly reused row and before its host-received KV is restored. `resume_retracted_reqs` had no such wait.

## Modifications

- `DecodePreallocQueue.resume_retracted_reqs`: under the overlap scheduler, make the scheduler stream wait for the forward stream before each `restore_kv_cache`. Both backends issue their copy after work on the scheduler stream (the `host_pool` copy waits on an event recorded there), so both are ordered after the forward that may still write the reused slots. As with the prebuilt path, this gives up overlap for the step in which a retracted request resumes; resuming is rare (after retraction under memory pressure).
- `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py`: the hand-built scheduler of `test_paged_swa_retraction_resume_uses_physical_page_budget` sets `enable_overlap=False`.
- Test `test_resumed_restore_lands_after_the_inflight_forward` in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_decode_retraction_backup.py` (CUDA). It uses real pools and a real `UnifiedRadixCache` with a host pool, and reproduces the interleaving deterministically:
  - a "forward" stream sleeps (`torch.cuda._sleep`) and then writes the slots that the resumed request is given;
  - `resume_retracted_reqs` then runs on the scheduler stream;
  - the restored KV must survive.
  On `main` the stale write lands after the restore and the test fails. A first pass with a short sleep loads every kernel first: CUDA lazy loading synchronizes the device on a kernel's first launch, which would otherwise order the race by accident.

Default behavior, not an option: the alternative is silent KV corruption, and the wait applies only in the iteration that resumes a retracted request.

This came out of auditing the retraction backup (`UnifiedRadixCache.backup_kv_cache`) for the overlap write-through race fixed in #42701. The backup is not exposed: it copies only `seqlen - 1` tokens, and the forward in flight at retraction writes only position `seqlen - 1`, so every copied position was written by a forward whose result the scheduler has already processed. The restore side, here, is exposed.

Out of scope: KV that the prefill server writes over RDMA into slots preallocated in the same iteration (`pop_preallocated`) is not ordered after the in-flight forward either. Transfer latency likely hides it, and I have not verified it.

Related: #42701 fences HiCache write-through copies for the same kind of race. The two PRs are independent and can merge in either order.

## Accuracy Tests

Not run end to end: reproducing this needs a PD deployment under enough memory pressure to retract and resume decode requests, and I did not set one up. The unit test above reproduces the interleaving on a GPU against the real pool, cache and restore code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The wait runs only in a scheduler iteration that resumes a retracted request.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Test results (RTX 5090, CUDA 13, torch 2.14.1, rebased on f2f0be731c):
- New test on `main`: fails, the restored KV is replaced by the in-flight write. With this PR: passes. Reproduced on two machines.
- `test_decode_retraction_backup.py` and `test/registered/unit/disaggregation`: 662 passed.
- Before the rebase, `test/registered/unit/managers` and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` matched `main` plus the new case; the one failure there (`test_mm_process_config.py::TestStreamOrderedMmFeaturePool::test_consumer_slot_uses_global_tp_rank`) also fails on `main` in the same environment.

@@ -17,6 +17,7 @@
 from sglang.srt.managers.scheduler_components.pool_stats_observer import (
     SchedulerPoolStatsObserver,
 )
+from sglang.srt.managers.utils import allocate_distinct_stream
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.allocator import (
     PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator,
     TokenToKVPoolAllocator,
@@ -702,6 +703,71 @@ def test_host_receive_restores_target_and_draft_kv(self, _world_size):
                 env.req_to_token_pool.free(req)
                 env.allocator.free(pressure)
 
+    @patch("torch.distributed.get_world_size", return_value=1)
+    def test_resumed_restore_lands_after_the_inflight_forward(self, _world_size):
+        """A request that finished last step can still have its forward in flight,
+        writing slots that a resumed request is given; the restore must land after
+        that write, or the stale write replaces the restored KV."""
+        env = self._build_cache(
+            hicache_ratio=2.0, shared_receive=True, draft_mode=HiCacheDraftMode.NONE
+        )
+        queue, _ = self._receive_queue(env)
+        engine = env.cache.cache_controller.l2_transfer_engine
+        # Pool streams can alias; an alias of the copy streams would order the race.
+        avoid = (engine.host_to_device_stream, engine.device_to_host_stream)
+        forward_stream = allocate_distinct_stream(torch.cuda, avoid)
+        queue.scheduler.enable_overlap = True
+        queue.scheduler.forward_stream = forward_stream
+        queue.scheduler.schedule_stream = allocate_distinct_stream(
+            torch.cuda, (*avoid, forward_stream)
+        )
+        buffers = (*env.target_pool.k_buffer, *env.target_pool.v_buffer)
+
+        def resume_behind_forward(forward_cycles):
+            req, source_indices = self._admit_req(env, self.num_tokens)
+            for buffer in buffers:
+                buffer[source_indices] = 7
+            req.kv.retraction_backup = env.cache.backup_kv_cache(req)
+            req.is_retracted = True
+            env.allocator.free(source_indices)
+            # Slots a finished request held, which its in-flight forward still writes.
+            reused = env.allocator.alloc(self.num_tokens)
+            for buffer in buffers:
+                buffer[reused] = 0
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            with torch.cuda.stream(queue.scheduler.forward_stream):
+                torch.cuda._sleep(forward_cycles)
+                # index_fill_ keeps the host free; a scalar setitem would sync on it.
+                for buffer in buffers:
+                    buffer.index_fill_(0, reused, -1)
+
+            def pre_alloc(resumed):
+                env.req_to_token_pool.write(
+                    (resumed.kv.req_pool_idx, slice(0, self.num_tokens)), reused
+                )
+
+            queue.retracted_queue = [req]
+            with (
+                patch.object(queue, "_uses_swa_reservation", return_value=False),
+                patch.object(queue, "_allocatable_token_budgets", return_value=1 << 20),
+                patch.object(queue, "_prealloc_required_tokens", return_value=(0, 0)),
+                patch.object(queue, "_prealloc_reservation_fits", return_value=True),
+                patch.object(queue, "_pre_alloc", side_effect=pre_alloc),
+                torch.cuda.stream(queue.scheduler.schedule_stream),
+            ):
+                self.assertEqual(queue.resume_retracted_reqs(), [req])
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            restored = [buffer[reused].clone() for buffer in buffers]
+            env.allocator.free(reused)
+            env.req_to_token_pool.free(req)
+            return restored
+
+        # CUDA lazy loading syncs the device on a kernel's first launch, which
+        # would order the race by accident; a first pass loads every kernel.
+        resume_behind_forward(forward_cycles=1)
+        for values in resume_behind_forward(forward_cycles=1 << 30):
+            self.assertTrue(torch.all(values == 7))
+
     @patch("torch.distributed.get_world_size", return_value=1)
     def test_host_receive_merges_existing_radix_prefix_after_restore(self, _world_size):
         """Receiving a cached prefix must not lock it or leak duplicate KV."""
